summary: On paper this one is close: Miami's best edge is to win short yardage (Miami's defense ranks 18th in short-yardage run success, 56% allowed), while Minnesota's best counter is to move people pre-snap (Minnesota ranks 27th in EPA per dropback with motion, +0.11). x-factor: Aaron Jones runs 0.5 yards per carry below expected, 11th of 12. The model favors Minnesota at 53%, mostly on home field (1.7 pts) and rushing matchup (1.4 pts).
